sections.label: Editions
sections.description: Fedora Editions are the official OS editions of Fedora Linux.

links.label: Workstation
links.description: The flagship Fedora edition featuring the latest Gnome desktop. The Linux desktop you've been waiting for.

links.label: Server
links.description: Run applications on bare metal or the cloud with a Linux server OS packed with the latest open source technology.

links.label: IoT
links.description: A foundation for Internet of Things and Device Edge ecosystem.

links.label: CoreOS
links.description: An automatically-updating, minimal operating system for running containerized workloads securely and at scale.

links.label: Cloud
links.description: An automatically-updating, minimal operating system for running containerized workloads securely and at scale.

sections.label: Emerging Editions
sections.description: These editions are supported but not yet a part of the official Fedora editions.

links.label: Silverblue
links.description: Fedora Silverblue is an immutable desktop operating system aimed at good support for container-focused workflows.

sections.label: Spins
sections.description: The Desktop spins feature specific Linux Desktop Environments. Our official Workstation Edition uses the Gnome Desktop, but you can install Fedora preconfigured with any of the listed Desktop Environments.

links.label: Fedora KDE
links.description: A complete, modern desktop built using the KDE Plasma Desktop Environment.

links.label: Fedora XFCE
links.description: A complete and well integrated desktop.

links.label: Cinnamon Desktop
links.description: A modern desktop featuring a traditional gnome user experience.

links.label: Mate-Compiz Desktop
links.description: A classic Fedora desktop with an additional 3D window manager.

links.label: i3 Tiling WM
links.description: Fedora Linux with the i3 Tiling Window Manager.

links.label: LXQT Desktop
links.description: A lightweight and well intgrated LXQT desktop environment.

links.label: LXDE Desktop
links.description: A light, fast, and less resource hungry desktop environment

links.label: Kinoite
links.description: Fedora Kinoite is an immutable KDE-based desktop.

sections.label: Labs
sections.description: The Labs are Fedora Linux set up with software bundles based on particular topics.

links.label: Astronomy
links.description: Powerful, completely open-source and free tools for amateur and professional astronomers.

links.label: Comp Neuro
links.description: A plethora of Free/Open source computational modelling tools for Neuroscience.

links.label: Design Suite
links.description: Visual design, multimedia production, and publishing suite of free and open source creative tools.

links.label: Games
links.description: A collection and perfect showcase of the best games available in Fedora.

links.label: Jam
links.description: For audio enthusiasts and musicians who want to create, edit, and produce audio and music on Linux.

links.label: Python Classroom
links.description: A classroom lab for teaching the Python programming language to students.

links.label: Robotics Suite
links.description: A wide variety of free and open robotics software packages for beginners and experts.

links.label: Scientific
links.description: A bundle of open source scientific and numerical tools used in research.

links.label: Security Lab
links.description: A bundle of open source scientific and numerical tools used in research.

community.label: Communities
community.description: Our community links connect you with our communication platforms, articles, blog posts, and events.

sections.label: Communications
sections.description: Our community is big and there are many ways that we connect with one another.

links.label: Fedora Discussion
links.description: The official Fedora messaging board. Chat with other Fedorans about our many community projects.

links.label: Fedora Matrix Chat
links.description: The official chat space of Fedora Linux. This link will help you get logged into Fedora Matrix.

links.label: Fedora Twitter
links.description: Follow us on twitter! This is a great place to stay up to date on the latest in the Fedora community.

links.label: Ask Fedora
links.description: Get help with your Fedora Operating System and learn more about the Fedora project on this official forum.

links.label: Mailing Lists
links.description: Subscribe to the mailing lists to stay up to date on Fedora's development discussions.

links.label: Fedora Mastodon
links.description: Follow us on Mastodon! This is a great place to stay up to date on the latest in the Fedora community.

sections.label: Publications
sections.description: The Fedora Project publishes content regularly in the Community Blog and Fedora Magazine. Stay up to date with the latest in the Fedora Community.

links.label: Fedora Magazine
links.description: Fedora Magazine publishes user friendly F/OSS guides and articles about Fedora Linux.

links.label: Community Blog
links.description: The Community Blog is used to share important news and updates about things happening in the Fedora community.

sections.label: Events
sections.description: From our release parties to our annual conference and more, Fedorans regularly come together to celebrate our community and the hard work that we put into it.

links.label: Flock To Fedora
links.description: The annual contributor conference for Fedora Linux. Flock takes place at the beginning of August.

links.label: Week of Diversity
links.description: This is a week in September where we highlight the contributions and experiences of women, lgbtq+, and bipoc in Fedora.

links.label: Release Parties
links.description: Fedora releases two major versions every year. We celebrate the hard work of our contributors virtually at each release.

sections.label: Extended Community
sections.description: Beyond the official channels for Fedorans to communicate, community members are involved on other popular platforms as well!

links.label: IRC
links.description: Prior to the move to Matrix, Fedrans officially chatted over IRC. Many IRC spaces are still maintained by the community.

links.label: Discord
links.description: This is a community managed Discord server for Fedora.

links.label: Telegram
links.description: Some SIG's in Fedora communicate over Telegram.

links.label: Reddit
links.description: This is a community managed subreddit for Fedora.
